surveys.title: Before we go any further — competition

questions.question: Write down your thoughts and feelings about competition. Are you a competitive person? How do you deal with competition? How do you feel when you win or when you lose?

Review your current and future competitor lists. Strike any names that don't fit the definition of competitor. Define your similarities and differences. Browse their websites, messaging, ads, and prices if available. What do they do well? Where are their shortcomings? Capture how you are sustainably different and what you learned objectively (not as a hater).

Who are your competitors?
questions.optionA: A company that provides the same or similar services that you do that has similar resources to you.
questions.optionB: A company that provides the same or similar services that you do that has way more or way less resources than you.

questions.question: Which of the following are features of a product?
questions.optionA: Statements about your product such as what it can do, its dimensions, specs, etc.
questions.optionB: The end result of what a product can actually accomplish for the customer

questions.question: What is the difference between benefit and value?
questions.optionA: Value corresponds to worth, whereas a product or service's benefit is all about what it can do for the customer
questions.optionB: Benefit corresponds to worth, whereas a product or service's value is all about what it can do for the customer

questions.question: Which of the following are types of market research?
questions.optionA: Numerical/quantitative, for example, analyzing statistics like demographics
questions.optionB: Qualitative, for example, conducting focus groups and surveys

questions.question: You need a lot of money and resources to conduct market research.
questions.optionA: TRUE, it can be really expensive to conduct market research.
questions.optionB: FALSE, there are more affordable ways to conduct market research such as reaching out to customers on social media and asking them what they think of your product.
